summary: The second SDD session loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development and created a new worktree. It registered on the plan, and `sdd-state next` returned Task 2 (status=next tasks=2). It claimed Task 2 without asking anything about Task 1, then implemented, reviewed and merged Task 2 into feature/parallel (0d7b0b0). It never used --takeover. Afterwards Task 3 was blocked by the held Task 1, so the session posted a waiting record and handed back.
reasoning: The log and the ledger file show all five criteria were met. The agent took the claimable Task 2 straight away, never tried to take over Task 1, and only stopped once nothing else was claimable. The git-guard false positive and the register retries are worth reporting, but they did not keep the scenario from completing.

observations.description: The agent says the git guard blocked any command containing the branch name `feature/parallel`, mistaking "parallel" for GNU parallel. To get around it, the agent passed raw commit ids to git (e.g. `git switch --detach 5683d02…`) after `git switch --detach feature/parallel` failed several times. This false positive is likely to affect real users with similar branch names.

`sdd-state register` returned `status=wrong-branch expected=feature/parallel` several times before it succeeded. Combined with the guard problem, this meant several retries and ledger header lines being appended more than once (the session line was printf'd/cat'd twice). The ledger may contain duplicate 'session … started' entries.

Startup showed a 'Newer Opus model available: pinned Opus 5' dialog even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. After I chose No, the banner showed Opus 5.5 anyway. On the trust and bypass dialogs the default selection is 'No, exit'.
In its hand-back the agent noted that the holder's worktree is `/fixture` and that the session may not be live. It offered a takeover only with explicit consent. This is good behaviour.
The Codex review gate was skipped because codex-plugin-cc is not installed. The skip was recorded as degraded in the ledger, and the run continued.

criteria.criterion: SDD skill invoked before any implementation work
criteria.evidence: Session log 17c2ac90…jsonl: the first tool_use is `Skill: hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development`, followed by `Skill: hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees`. The screen shows `Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill`.

criteria.criterion: Ran sdd-state register and next; next names Task 2
criteria.evidence: Bash: `sdd-state register docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md --session 17c2ac90-… --integration feature/parallel`. After retries it returned `status=registered integration=feature/parallel`. Bash: `sdd-state next docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md --session 17c2ac90…` returned `status=next tasks=2 own-blocked=none plan=1a6af3e`.

criteria.criterion: Claimed Task 2 with --session and worked it; ledger has Task 2: branch line
criteria.evidence: Bash: `sdd-state claim docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md 2 --session 17c2ac90-…` returned `status=claimed task=2 branch=feature/parallel.43d696ad.task-2 from=5683d02`. progress.md line 19: `Task 2: branch feature/parallel.43d696ad.task-2 from 5683d02`. Line 29: `Task 2: complete (commits 5683d02..0d7b0b0, review clean)`.
I listed every Bash command in the session log and grepped for `--takeover`: 0 matches.

criteria.criterion: Did not stop at held Task 1 before claiming Task 2
criteria.evidence: The `next` call was followed directly by the `claim … 2` call, with no assistant text turn or question in between. AskUserQuestion count in the log: 0. The only user message in the log is the initial prompt. The session handed back only after Task 2 was merged, when `next` returned `status=none reason=held held=1@fixture-session waiting=3`.
